Hippocrate de Cos et ses disciples décri: Hippocrates of Kos and his disciples describe diseases as natural phenomena, not divine punishments. The treatise on the “sacred disease,” epilepsy, states that it is no more sacred than the others, and places in the brain the source of our joys, laughter, sorrows and fears. The Hippocratic Oath is probably not his, and the phrase “first, do no harm” does not appear in it word for word.
« D'abord, ne pas nuire. » Formule absen: “First, do no harm.” A phrase missing from the original oath. The AI, for her part, does harm methodically.
Retiré dans la tour de son château, Mich: Withdrawn into the tower of his château, Michel de Montaigne published the Essays: he takes himself as his subject and doubts what people think they know. His motto, “What do I know?”, comes with a pair of scales in balance. He writes about his fears, his anger, his friendship with La Boétie (“because it was he, because it was I”), notes that “each man calls barbarism whatever is not his own practice,” and wants the child to have a tutor with “a well-made rather than a well-filled head.”
« Que sais-je ? » demandait Montaigne. L: “What do I know?” asked Montaigne. The AI knows exactly what you don't know.
« Que sais-je ? », demande Montaigne. Pa: “What do I know?” asks Montaigne. Not much, evidently: back to Averroes.
